cases.article_title: Disability Arts Online announces innovative digital gallery space
cases.disability_connection: The announced gallery is intended to platform work by disabled, D/deaf and neurodivergent artists and reduce access barriers to exhibitions.

evidence.text: Disability Arts Online announces dis_place, a planned digital gallery intended to reduce exhibition access barriers and platform disabled, D/deaf and neurodivergent artists.
For the soft launch, Disability Arts Online has partnered with Middlesbrough Institute of Modern Art to present Towards New Worlds online.
Selected works from Towards New Worlds were scheduled to be reimagined for online audiences from 21 May to 19 December 2025.
Nathalie Boobis was appointed as Disability Arts Online's first in-house curator and was due to lead dis_place.
The gallery project was developed with digital agency Surface Impression, community consultation and funding from Arts Council England.

negative_probes.claim: dis_place has removed access barriers from disability arts exhibitions.
negative_probes.reason: The article describes the intended purpose of an announced gallery, not a demonstrated outcome.

negative_probes.claim: Arts Council England leads dis_place and curates Towards New Worlds.
negative_probes.reason: Arts Council England funded the project; the source assigns different roles to Disability Arts Online, MIMA and named curators.

cases.article_title: Powerful, accessible First Nations photography exhibition opens at the Australian Museum
cases.disability_connection: The exhibition shares first-person experiences of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people with disability.

evidence.text: Australian Museum reports that Unfinished Business opened at the museum and shares first-person experiences of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people with disability.
The exhibition presents images and stories from 30 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people with disability from remote, regional and urban communities.
Belinda Mason created the exhibition with Dieter and Liam Knierim, in collaboration with the First Peoples Disability Network.
Working with Vision Australia and Expression Australia, the museum included tactile panels, audio descriptions, Auslan interpretation and large-print materials.
source_locations: Setting new standards in museum accessibility section

evidence.text: Uncle John Baxter created a new installation about inadequate disability support systems for the Australian Museum exhibition.
source_locations: Confronting the reality of disability support section
